title: River Delta Sediment Deposition Branching
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D river delta sediment deposition and branching simulation using Three.js and GLTFLoader.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 60, 80) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (30, 50, 20) with intensity 0.8 and shadow mapping enabled.
- Create a flat terrain plane (200x200) using a MeshStandardMaterial with a sandy color (#C2B280). The terrain is subdivided into a 100x100 grid so vertex heights can be modified by sediment accumulation.
- Load the asset 'coffeemat.glb' using GLTFLoader. Scale it to (0.3, 0.3, 0.3) and place it at the river source point (0, 1, -90) as a decorative 'sediment source marker'. Store its reference in window.__3D_STATE__.sourceMarker.
- OrbitControls for camera.

## Water / River System
- The river originates from the top-center of the terrain (0, 0.2, -90) and flows toward positive Z (downward on the plane).
- Represent the river as a set of particle streams (small blue spheres, radius 0.15). Particles flow from source toward +Z with a base velocity of 0.5 units/frame.
- When a particle reaches a branching point (every 30 units along Z starting at Z=-60), it randomly branches left or right with a spread angle between 10-35 degrees. This creates a delta pattern.
- Maximum 5 branching generations (depth). Each branch can split into 2 sub-branches.
- Store all active branch paths in window.__3D_STATE__.branches as an array of objects: {id, startPos:{x,y,z}, endPos:{x,y,z}, angle, generation, active, particleCount}.

## Sediment Deposition
- Each water particle deposits sediment as it travels. Sediment accumulates on the terrain vertices nearest to the particle path.
- Track total sediment deposited as window.__3D_STATE__.totalSediment (starts at 0, increments by 0.01 per particle per frame).
- The terrain mesh vertex Y values increase where sediment accumulates, visually building up the delta.
- Track the maximum terrain height as window.__3D_STATE__.maxTerrainHeight.
- Sediment mass is conserved: totalSediment === sum of all vertex height increases (within epsilon 0.05).

## Simulation Controls
- A 'Play/Pause' button (id='btn-play-pause') toggles simulation. window.__3D_STATE__.running (boolean, starts true).
- A 'Reset' button (id='btn-reset') resets all sediment, branches, particles, terrain to initial state.
- A 'Flow Rate' slider (id='slider-flow-rate', range 0.1 to 2.0, step 0.1, default 1.0) multiplies particle spawn rate. Expose as window.__3D_STATE__.flowRate.
- A 'Branch Probability' slider (id='slider-branch-prob', range 0.1 to 1.0, step 0.05, default 0.5) controls likelihood of branching at each branch point. Expose as window.__3D_STATE__.branchProbability.
- Keyboard 'S' key: take a snapshot of current state into window.__3D_STATE__.snapshot (deep copy of branches, totalSediment, maxTerrainHeight, flowRate, branchProbability).
- Keyboard 'U' key: undo/restore from snapshot — revert branches, totalSediment, terrain heights, flowRate, branchProbability to snapshot values.
- Keyboard 'ArrowUp'/'ArrowDown': increase/decrease flowRate by 0.1 (clamped to slider range).

## HUD
- A HUD overlay div (id='hud') in top-left showing:
  - Active Branches: count (id='hud-branches')
  - Total Sediment: value to 2 decimals (id='hud-sediment')
  - Max Height: value to 2 decimals (id='hud-max-height')
  - Flow Rate: value (id='hud-flow-rate')
  - Status: Running/Paused (id='hud-status')

## State Object (window.__3D_STATE__)
Expose on window.__3D_STATE__:
- running: boolean
- flowRate: number
- branchProbability: number
- totalSediment: number
- maxTerrainHeight: number
- branches: array of branch objects
- activeBranchCount: number (computed, branches with active===true)
- particleCount: number (total active water particles in scene)
- sourceMarkerLoaded: boolean (true once coffeemat.glb loaded)
- snapshot: object or null
- snapshotRestored: boolean (set true after U key restore, reset to false on next S key)
- terrainVertexSum: number (sum of all terrain vertex Y displacements, should equal totalSediment within epsilon)
- simulationTime: number (frames elapsed since start, paused frames don't count)
- resetCount: number (how many times reset was pressed, starts 0)

All values must be updated every frame. Ensure no NaN values in any numeric field.
physics_constraints: Sediment mass conservation: totalSediment must equal terrainVertexSum within epsilon 0.05. Particles must flow in +Z direction only. Branch angles must be between 10-35 degrees. Flow rate clamped [0.1, 2.0]. Branch generation depth max 5. No NaN in any state field. Terrain height monotonically non-decreasing at any vertex (sediment only accumulates, never erodes). Snapshot restore must exactly match saved values.
